text:
alina: quick check — I'm proposing a small slab-fusion prototype to reduce fragmentation for tiny prefixes (<= 8KB). idea: fuse adjacent small slabs into a fusion slab with per-tenant tags so we can still evict at tenant granularity. thoughts?

 dexter: sounds promising. main risk i see is eviction correctness when a tenant in the fusion slab gets tombstoned. how do we avoid evicting another tenant's live keys?

 alina: plan is to keep a per-slab metadata table with (tenant_id -> reference_count, lease_token). eviction would require acquiring the slab-level lease and decrementing refs for that tenant only. if ref_count hits 0 for the tenant we physically reclaim those entries.

 maria: hmm refcounts are fine but atomicity of ref decrement + reclaim is tricky across nodes. what's our cross-node handoff if the lease holder dies mid-reclaim?

 alina: good point. we'll do a two-phase reclaim: 1) mark tenant entries as "reclaimable" in slab metadata (fast, idempotent) 2) background compaction that physically frees items only after confirming no active leases for that tenant on the node. mark is cheap and replicated.

 chen: does marking need a global epoch? otherwise another node might interpret mark differently and rehydrate prefix during a read.

 dexter: we should include an epoch on the slab metadata. mark writes current epoch and a uuid of the reclaim op. reads see mark+epoch and if they have a newer lease they ignore it.

 alina: yep proposing slab_epoch + reclaim_uuid. also adding an invariant assert: readers refuse to serve stale items if slab_epoch < lease_epoch. we'll instrument failures.

 tomas: what about performance? fusion adds indirection (lookup by offset) — any perf numbers?

 alina: microbench on my laptop: fused slab lookup ~5% slower p95 for single-key gets, but mem efficiency improves ~18% for workloads with many <8KB prefixes. should be OK for low-priority tenants.

 maria: is there an operator knob to disable fusion per-tenant? we don't want premium tenants on fused slabs accidentally.

 alina: yes, tenant opt-out flag and automatic policy: use fusion for tenants with median prefix size <= 6KB and traffic < X qps.

 dexter: how do rollbacks look if fusion causes correctness bugs in canary? need kill-switch and safe rollback path.

 alina: rollout plan: feature flag + canary on one slab range per region. if we need to rollback we flip flag and start compaction to split fused slabs back to per-tenant slabs. compaction is idempotent: it creates new small slabs and migrates live entries.

 chen: split compaction needs to preserve ordering for cursors/long-lived reads. any plan for cursor semantics?

 alina: cursors track (slab_id, offset, lease_epoch). compaction will keep mapping table so old cursors can be rewritten to new slab/offset — it's a background migration that keeps redirects for N minutes. we'll also return HTTP 409 to cursors that land in the redirect window to force retry.

 maria: what metrics should we add to catch silent correctness issues?

 alina: add: "slab_fusion_reclaims", "slab_fusion_compactions", "slab_fusion_reclaim_conflicts", "slab_epoch_mismatch_errors", and a high-cardinality sample log for reclaim_uuid failures (sample 1/1000).

 ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary build 1771.2 pushed to canary cluster eu-west-1 at 1771002245. CI: unit tests 122 passed, integration smoke basic-prefetch failed 1/12 — investigating.

 dexter: ping @alina for the integration smoke failure — any test gap we expect?

 alina: the smoke failure is in eviction race sim — i forgot to add epoch bump in the simulated reclaim path. fixing and running smoke again.

 maria: after you fix, let's run the chaos test that force-kills nodes mid-reclaim. also add a test that simulates concurrent reads during compaction that rehydrate a prefix from origin storage.

 alina: agreed. i'll push a patch tonight with: epoch bump in sim, compaction redirect mapping, and the new metrics. then we can enable canary on one more slab range.

 chen: overall this feels workable. just be explicit in the RFC followup about the invariants we rely on (lease_epoch monotonicity, reclaim_uuid uniqueness) and the operator playbook for rollback.

 alina: will do. i'll draft a concise RFC follow-up with diagrams and the operator steps (canary flag, compaction-split command, metric thresholds). expecting to post by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup: 

 tomas: thanks — ping if you want an ops review of the playbook before posting.

 alina: thanks all, will update thread when RFC follow-up is up.
